No source combines Schelling relocation with a cyclic or excitable CA in which the vacant state is a step of the cycle. In the closest relatives, type switching is random and between two types (Hazan) or voter-like (Caridi), and mobility is local exchange (the rock-paper-scissors papers).
Not covered: Schelling-level coarsening (domains and interfaces) that survives continual coherent cycling at intermediate activity, with vacancies created and destroyed by the cycle.
The combination effect rests on the activity feature alone, because domains and interfaces are statistically indistinguishable from Schelling only (within about one spread). The global composition oscillation seen in the re-run is not among the verified features and would need its own check.
review:051.citation_problems: Nothing material. All six URLs resolve to real works that support the background claims they are used for. The MCell page could not be re-checked because the host is down. The citations are bare URLs with no mapping to claims.

census:novelty:network-2.basis:
Vilone, Ramasco, Sanchez & San Miguel 2014, 'Social imitation versus strategic choice, or consensus versus cooperation, in the networked Prisoner's Dilemma', PRE 90:022810 (arXiv 1405.4997). They mix unconditional imitation (copy the best neighbour) with social imitation (the voter model) on the same PD strategy, on Erdos-Renyi and scale-free networks. Each rule alone freezes or reaches consensus. With unconditional imitation, a region of parameter space (high social-imitation rate, low punishment, i.e. near the weak PD) stays in a persistent dynamic state: active-link density stays non-zero and consensus time grows exponentially with N ('the fate of the system is not frozen but a dynamic state').
Payoff imitation combined with majority conformity on the strategy itself, on networks: Pena, Pestelacci, Tomassini & Volken 2009 (IEEE CEC; PRE 80:016110); Wang, Zhu & Ren 2012 (Sci China PMA 55:1225), where the update uses both payoff differences and the neighbours' majority; and Szolnoki & Perc 2015 (J R Soc Interface 12:20141299), where conformists add an effective surface tension around cooperator clusters.
The modularity feature is standard network reciprocity under imitate-the-best (Nowak-May; Szabo & Fath 2007).
census:novelty:network-2.difference:
Vilone et al.'s social imitation is the voter model, not majority rule, and they apply one rule or the other on each update (probability q). Here every node imitates the best each step and then conforms to the majority with probability 0.1. The conformity papers do use majority rule, but they report cooperation levels and cluster shapes, not sustained turnover. Not covered: persistent turnover produced by majority-rule conformity against deterministic imitate-the-best on a random graph.
Caveat for the simulation check: the census compares frames 10 steps apart, which hides period-2 blinking. A reviewer re-run of census/sim.py (4 seeds) shows that imitation alone already has 9-16% of nodes changing every step, with lag-2 change of only 0-7%. Part of the activity 'interaction effect' is therefore the majority step breaking this period-2 locking into aperiodic churn.
Stage 3's twist (conformity acting on a label separate from the strategy) does not exist in the code: the majority rule acts on the strategy itself, which is exactly the documented conformity setting.
census:novelty:network-2.citation_problems: One misattribution: 'Conformity and Network Effects in the Prisoner's Dilemma' is by Pena, Pestelacci, Tomassini & Volken (IEEE CEC 2009), not Pacheco et al. The tag-model citations (Kim 2010; Jensen & Bornholdt 2019) support a 'separate label' framing that does not apply, because in the simulator the node type is the strategy. Stage 3 missed the closest source (Vilone et al. 2014).

qd:037.basis:
Hazan & Randon-Furling 2013, 'A Schelling model with switching agents', EPJ B 86:421 (arXiv 1212.4929). It is the same coupling class: Schelling relocation to random vacancies plus a fraction of spatially fixed agents that switch type, which gives intermediate patterns (a mixture of patches, fuzzy interfaces) instead of full separation.
Gauvin, Vannimenus & Nadal 2010, 'Schelling segregation in an open city' (PRE 81:066120, arXiv 1002.3758): vacancy density is set endogenously by the agent dynamics through a chemical-potential-like parameter. This is a related setting where occupancy is not conserved.
Gauvin et al. 2009 (EPJ B 70:293) and Abella, San Miguel & Ramasco 2022 (Sci Rep) document the tolerance-vacancy phase diagram, which explains why the Schelling-only run at threshold 0.2 is static.
qd:037.difference:
In Hazan & Randon-Furling the switching agents sit at sites that are never empty, switch at random between the two types, never relocate, and conserve both the number of agents of each class and the vacancy density. Here the switching cycle passes through the empty state, and the occupant of a switching site can relocate before it is switched off. That makes a ratchet: agents leave switching sites while occupied, escaping the type 2 -> empty step, and each vacated site is refilled at once, so vacancies fall by about 90%.
No source found describes this vacancy pumping or its result, Schelling dynamics running at about 3% vacancies with two nearly equal types. In the open city, occupancy changes through satisfaction-based entry and exit, not through a ratchet at fixed sites.
Of the verified features, the type-entropy drop and roughly half the domain-count reduction are composition effects of the pump rather than spatial organisation, and the reversals are largely built into the cycling sites. Stage 3 identified the pump correctly.
qd:037.citation_problems: None: all four resolve and the quoted phrases were found in the full texts. A minor point: the 'freezes in a disordered state' quote is about low tolerance in the accepted-unlike convention, and the 0.2 threshold here sits at the high-tolerance (mixed or static) end, which Stage 3 acknowledges only in passing.
